title: Primitive Triangulation: Prove exists_reduction constructively
question: Can the axiom `exists_reduction` in PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01.lean be proved constructively, removing it as an assumption? The axiom states: for any lattice triangle with |det| > 1, there exist T1, T2 with |det(T1)| + |det(T2)| = |det(T)| and both positive.

insights: The axiom statement has no geometric constraint (T1, T2 need not sub-triangulate T), only det-value constraints — enabling a trivial constructive witness
Unit triangle (0,0),(1,0),(0,1) has det=1; elongated triangle (0,0),(n-1,0),(0,1) has det=n-1
Int.natAbs_natCast converts (↑k : ℤ).natAbs to k for k : ℕ
Strong induction (Nat.strongRecOn) on |det| cleanly handles the recursive structure
builtItems: exists_reduction proved as theorem (PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01.lean:115-142) — removes axiom
nextSteps: Consider strengthening exists_reduction to require geometric sub-triangulation
Investigate if any edge of a lattice triangle with |det|>1 always has gcd>1 (enabling Section III's splitLeft/splitRight)
knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: axiom removed, exists_reduction proved constructively, 0 axioms remain
